assertion.statement: Plain correlation of Delta_h f with a globally bounded internal family gives plain bias for a positive N^3 number of the exact shifted additive quadruples.
assertion.objects: Finite J=[N], I=[-N,N], M=J+I, K=[-2N,2N], zero-extended f and globally defined chi_h.
assertion.hypotheses: Positive density alpha, uniformly positive correlation delta, fixed global bound B and finite component dimension.
assertion.quantifiers: Every positive N, every such family and all integer arguments of chi_h; the conclusion selects distinct quadruples.
assertion.parameter_range: No nilsequence or degree hypothesis is required. Section13 applies it to a full scalar component retaining its lower nilcharacter factor.
assertion.uniformity: Threshold and count constants depend only on alpha,delta,B and the fixed finite vector dimension, never N.
assertion.constants: a=alpha delta/3, eta=a^4/4; at least eta/(2B^4) of K times I squared have correlation at least eta/2.
assertion.normalizations: Both displayed domain transfers are exact; the second Cauchy-Schwarz removes the bounded weight f(n-k) by inequality, not by dropping a support factor in an equality.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Complex phases preserve absolute correlation; vector reduction uses finite pigeonhole and no division by components; all N>=1 covered.
assertion.limit_order: Fix uniform bounds and finite assignments, prove the finite inequality, then take ultralimits. No inverse or factorization theorem is used.
